newsitem.title: USA: Detroit gunman killed after he kills 3, wounds 2.
newsitem.headline: Detroit gunman killed after he kills 3, wounds 2.

text.p: Reciting the Lord's Prayer while he fired a shotgun, a man dressed in camouflage killed two bank employees and a hostage Tuesday during a robbery attempt before police shot him dead in a hail of bullets.
The rampage also left two wounded, including a young male jogger the gunman shot in the face at random on the street before entering the bank, police said.

The gunman, identified only as an African American male in his early 20s wearing gray-and-white camouflage and matching cap, then drove a stolen car about two blocks to the Comerica Bank on Detroit's East Side. Once inside, he demanded money and began muttering incoherent religious statements, police said.

"He walked in with a shotgun and forced patrons and employees to lie on the floor," Detroit Police Chief Isiah McKinnon said. "He forced them to recite the Lord's Prayer. He was reciting it with them as he was shooting."
The gunman shot and killed two male employees and wounded a female employee in the chin after police, notified when a silent alarm was tripped, surrounded the bank.

Killed inside the bank were the branch office's manager, Stanley Pijanowski III, 52, and James Isom, 25, a retail services representative. Wounded was assistant branch manager Lisa Griffin, 38, who was listed in fair condition at St. John Hospital and Medical Centre in Detroit.
The identity of a hostage killed outside the bank, a customer, was not yet available. Nor was the name of the 23-year-old jogger made available.
Charlene McDonald, who was in the bank with her children to cash a check, told WXYZ-TV that she watched in terror as the gunman killed Pijanowski and Isom.

"He cocked his gun, and he shot, but it didn't go off," McDonald said. "So when he did it again, I looked over there to see who he was going to shoot, but the person was laying on their side, and when he got ready to shoot, they closed their eyes and put their hand up there (over their face) and he just shot 'em in the head."
"Before he got to me, he shot somebody else," McDonald said, adding that she managed to escape unhurt when the gunman turned his head.
The gunman left the bank and fled into an alley, taking with him as hostage a man who was using an automatic teller machine.

Deputy Police Chief Benny Napoleon said the gunman, holding the hostage by the neck, fired at police several times, but added that police did not return fire because they did not want to injure the hostage.

"He then shot, fatally wounded, the hostage that he had taken at the automatic teller machine, he shot him in the head," Napoleon told reporters. "At that point in time, the police officers fatally wounded the perpetrator."
Some witnesses at the scene said the gunman shot the hostage after he apparently tried to break free. At that instant, witnesses said scores of police officers opened fire on the gunman.

At St. John Hospital and Medical Centre in Detroit, the 23-year-old man shot in the face was listed in serious condition, and a 38-year-old woman shot inside the bank was listed in fair condition, a spokeswoman said.
Another woman not injured in the incident who was believed to be pregnant also was treated and released by the hospital.

Thomas Fisher, Comerica Bank senior vice president, said the branch has been the victim of attempted robberies in the past, but said the robbery Tuesday "does not seem to fit the mould of anything I've ever seen before."
He said he did not know whether additional security measures would have prevented the tragedy, adding, "From what I've been told so far, we're dealing with a deranged gunman."
